notes: Personality archetypes borrowed from Perfect Dark's special simulants. These are orthogonal to skill: a personality says what a bot WANTS, a skill tier says how well it executes.

The design insight worth stealing is that most of these are not difficulty settings at all -- they are opponents that behave in a legible, exploitable way. A bot that always runs for armour is not harder than one that does not, it is a different puzzle, and that is what makes a lobby of mixed simulants interesting to play against rather than merely hard.

Several of them are also deliberately WEAK. Rare shipped opponents that flee, refuse to shoot, or throw themselves at you, because variety of behaviour matters more to a match than uniform competence. That is the opposite of the instinct to make every bot as strong as possible.
Every opcode named here is checked against src/bondaicommands.h by tools/gen_bot_archetypes.py.

archetypes.name: peace
archetypes.summary: Refuses to shoot. Runs from fights and strips the arena of weapons and ammunition so nobody else can arm themselves.
behaviour: Never fires a weapon; will attempt to disarm anyone who closes to melee range.
Hoovers up weapons and ammunition ahead of the players, which is a denial strategy rather than a pacifist one.
Flees on contact instead of engaging.

archetypes.name: shield
archetypes.summary: Obsessed with armour. Always heads for it, and breaks off to get another the moment its own is dented.
behaviour: Routes to armour before weapons, even while unarmed.
Abandons a fight it is winning if its armour takes any damage.
Effectively concedes control of everything except the armour spawn, which makes it predictable.

archetypes.name: kaze
archetypes.summary: Suicidally fearless. Charges regardless of what it is holding or how much health it has left.
behaviour: Closes to contact range at a sprint and never retreats.
Ignores its own health entirely; will charge at a sliver.
Dangerous out of proportion to its accuracy, because it removes the option of a ranged trade.

archetypes.name: fist
archetypes.summary: Melee only. Never fires a projectile weapon and closes to punching range instead.
behaviour: Sprints directly at its target and attacks by hand.
Harder to hit than it should be, because auto-aim does not assist against an unarmed opponent.
That last property is the reason it is interesting rather than a joke -- it exploits a real mechanic.

archetypes.name: prey
archetypes.summary: A bully. Only attacks the weak -- low health, freshly respawned, or badly armed -- and ignores anyone dangerous.
behaviour: Selects targets by weakness rather than by proximity.
Actively avoids armoured or well-armed opponents.
Punishes respawns, which makes spawn position matter to the human players too.

archetypes.name: coward
archetypes.summary: Avoids confrontation. Flees at the first sign of a fight and only engages when it holds the better weapon.
behaviour: Breaks contact immediately unless it has a weapon advantage.
Spends the match collecting rather than fighting.
Frustrating to hunt on a large map, which is a design feature rather than a flaw.

archetypes.name: judge
archetypes.summary: Attacks whoever is winning. A self-balancing opponent that suppresses the leader and switches targets as the score changes.
behaviour: Target selection is driven by the scoreboard rather than by the arena.
If it takes the lead itself, it attacks everyone to keep it.
Keeps matches close without any explicit rubber-banding, which is a far more elegant solution than scaling difficulty.

archetypes.name: feud
archetypes.summary: Picks one opponent at the start and hunts only them for the whole match, ignoring everyone else.
behaviour: Chooses a rival once and never reconsiders.
Walks past other players to reach its target.
Turns a free-for-all into an asymmetric match, which changes the game for everyone rather than only its victim.

archetypes.name: venge
archetypes.summary: Holds grudges. Hunts whoever killed it last, switching targets each time it dies.
behaviour: Re-targets on every death, so its attention follows whoever is doing well against it.
Effectively punishes a player who kills it repeatedly.
Reads as personality rather than as scripting, which is the whole trick.

archetypes.name: speed
archetypes.summary: Roughly twice normal movement speed, and the same speed at every skill tier.
behaviour: Fast enough to be genuinely hard to track with anything slow-firing.
Its speed does not scale with skill, so a low-skill one is still evasive and a high-skill one is brutal.
Best countered with area weapons rather than precision ones.

archetypes.name: turtle
archetypes.summary: The inverse of speed: moves much slower than a player but carries roughly double the usual armour.
behaviour: Absorbs a great deal of fire, so it wins attrition fights it should lose.
Easy to escape from and hard to remove, which makes it an area-denial opponent.
Pairs the two dials against each other, which is why it plays differently rather than just being tankier.

archetypes.name: rocket
archetypes.summary: Uses explosives exclusively, which makes it lethal in the open and a danger to itself in corridors.
behaviour: Only ever engages with explosive weapons.
Extremely strong on the open arenas and close to self-defeating in the tight ones.
Its strength is therefore a property of the map rather than of the bot, which is a useful thing for a lobby to be able to tune.
